body:
### Summary

Hello,
First of all thank you for your amazing work on UV, it has made our life so much easier, all of my team's scripts are uvx tools now !
The following "bug" could very well be a skill issue on my part, feel free to point me to the correct answer if this is the case.

### Description
I have noticed that uvx behaves differently when run inside or outside of a project.

Let's say that I have published to pypi my_awesome_tool.
This tool depends explicitely on fastapi version 0.120.0 in the pyproject.toml (strict == requirement)
The package is published with uv build && uv publish

If I run uvx my_awesome_tool in a random directory, everything works fine, fastapi version 0.120.0 is used.
But if I run uvx my_awesome_tool from a subdirectory of a python project, this project's dependencies will be used instead, **even if they don't match my_awesome_tool requirements**

e.g running it from a subdirectory of a project that has fastapi version 0.136.0 will use fastapi v0.136.0 instead of version 0.120.0.

I have not enabled the venv in my terminal in any way.

### Expected result
I would expect by default uvx to ignore any parent venv/pyproject, unless explicitely specified.

If that is actually the intended behavior, I would advise to check before that the tool's dependency requirements constraints are satisfied. i.e if the tool depends on fastapi 0.120.0 explicitely, it should not be using the project's fastapi version 0.136.0, it should at the very least raise an error.

### What about the isolated flag ?
Oddly, running uvx with the --isolated flag also exhibits the same behavior, even if the python imports resolve to the uv cache location this time instead of the project's venv

### Reproducibility
#### Create a tool :
```toml
[project]
name = "mytool"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "Dummy."
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi[standard]==0.120.0",
]

[project.scripts]
mytool = "mytool.main:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build<=0.12"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[tool.uv.build-backend]
module-name = ["mytool"]
module-root = ""
```

Add the following to the main.py to help debug the import location:
```python
import sys
import fastapi

def main():
    for name, mod in sorted(sys.modules.items()):
        # Skip modules that don't have a file path (like built-ins or internal modules)
        if mod is not None and hasattr(mod, "__file__") and mod.__file__ is not None:
            print(f"{name:<30} | {mod.__file__}")
```

#### Test and publish it :
uv run mytool
uv build && uv publish

#### Use a newer fastapi version locally
Increment the package version in pyproject.toml and set the fastapi version requirement to 0.136.0
Update the .venv directory with uv sync.

#### Run uvx in and out of the project
uvx mytool # from the project : uses fastapi 0.136.0
cd ../ && uvx mytool  #  uses fastapi 0.120.0

Thank you for your help !



### Platform

RHEL9.6, Linux 5.14.0-570.58.1.el9_6.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.12.1 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

3.12.9
title: uvx should not use the project's dependencies
